title: Power Apps: prompt columns can store multiple lines of text output
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, licensing statements and general prompt-column controls are supported. The documented organization endpoint supports updating the AI prompts setting, while the multi-line feature's default and configuration details remain unpublished.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters
claims.claim: The planned change allows prompt columns to store multiple lines of prompt output for longer, more detailed AI-generated text.
claims.quote: Prompt columns can now store multilple lines of text as prompt output, enabling longer and detailed AI-generated insights to be stored in your tables.

claims.claim: The roadmap lists Power Apps and Microsoft Dataverse.
claims.quote: "products": ["Power Apps", "Microsoft Dataverse"]

claims.claim: The roadmap status is In development.
claims.quote: "status": "In development", "statusKey": "in-development"

claims.where: front matter: targetDate; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap target is November CY2026, presented as a target rather than a commitment.
claims.quote: "targetDate": "November CY2026"

claims.where: front matter: releasePhase; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), GCC and GCC High.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)", "GCC", "GCC High"]

claims.where: front matter: platforms; What's changing; Scope; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Web is the only platform listed in the roadmap record.
claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.claim: The roadmap gives no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.claim: A prompt column is an AI-powered Dataverse data type.
claims.quote: A prompt column is an AI-powered data type in Microsoft Dataverse

claims.claim: A prompt column holds results of natural language prompts tied to other columns in the table.
claims.quote: enables you to define natural language prompts tied to other columns in your table. The AI model processes these prompts to generate relevant responses based on specified input columns.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Generated prompt-column results persist in the Dataverse table.
claims.quote: The key function is that the prompt column contains generative AI results stored in the table persistently.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: A prompt executes automatically when a record is created.
claims.quote: A prompt executes when you create a record or update one or more of the columns that the prompt references.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: A prompt executes when one or more referenced columns are updated.
claims.quote: A prompt executes when you create a record or update one or more of the columns that the prompt references.

claims.claim: The Learn prompt-columns page does not describe multi-line output.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" output default limit; "prompt columns" "multi-line" admin existing licensing rollout. Opened Prompt columns; no multi-line output section or configuration was present.

claims.claim: How multi-line output is selected is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" output default limit; "prompt columns" "multi-line" admin existing licensing rollout. Opened Prompt columns and its creation and editing instructions; no multi-line selection control was stated.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: No source states whether the multi-line change alters existing prompt columns.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multi-line" admin existing licensing rollout. Opened Prompt columns and Specialized columns using code; existing-column upgrade statements concern asynchronous execution, not multi-line output.

claims.claim: A length limit specifically for multi-line prompt-column output is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Power Apps prompt columns multiline output November 2026 573279 default length limit. Read Prompt columns and search excerpts for Types of columns and Create and edit columns; general text limits do not identify this planned output.

claims.claim: Rollout mechanics for multi-line prompt-column output are not stated.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multi-line" admin existing licensing rollout. Read the roadmap record and Prompt columns; rollout notes on Learn concern asynchronous computation and bulk processing, not multi-line output.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: The arrival default of the multi-line output change is unknown.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" output default limit; Power Apps prompt columns multiline output November 2026 573279 default length limit. Read the roadmap and Prompt columns; neither states the multi-line arrival default.

claims.claim: No new admin switch specifically for multi-line output is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" licensing default switch; "prompt columns" "multi-line" admin existing licensing rollout. Opened Prompt columns, Administer AI Builder and Manage feature settings; no multi-line-specific switch was found.

claims.claim: Prompt-column licensing is consumption-based.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume credits every time a prompt is executed.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Prompt columns use the same licensing model as AI Builder prompts.
claims.quote: Prompt columns use the same licensing model as AI builder prompts.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The prompts overview lists Copilot Credits as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: You need Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: The prompts overview requires Dataverse to be installed in the environment.
claims.quote: Microsoft Dataverse is installed on the environment.

claims.claim: The prompts overview requires an environment in an available region.
claims.quote: Your environment is in the list of available regions.

claims.claim: Prompt columns support AI Builder credits.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume both AI Builder credits and Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Prompt columns support Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume both AI Builder credits and Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Learn notes that AI Builder credits are retiring soon.
claims.quote: AI Builder credits are retiring soon.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: AI Builder features in apps and flows try AI Builder credits first and then Copilot Credits when AI Builder credits are absent or exhausted.
claims.quote: AI Builder features in apps and flows first try to consume AI Builder credits, then if absent or exhausted, they try to consume Copilot Credits.

claims.claim: Prompt columns consume credits every time a prompt executes.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume credits every time a prompt is executed.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Testing a prompt in the designer is free.
claims.quote: Testing a prompt is free. The credits on lower right are estimates for one run.

claims.claim: The AI Builder activity report for prompt-column credit monitoring is in Power Automate's Automation center.
claims.quote:
Sign in to Power Automate.
On the left navigation pane, select Automation center, and then select AI Builder activity.

claims.claim: Estimated consumption shows the credits consumed by each prompt execution.
claims.quote: Review the Estimated consumption column to see the credits consumed by each prompt execution.

claims.claim: Filter conditions reduce unnecessary prompt executions and help optimise credit consumption.
claims.quote: During record creation or update, the prompt column evaluates the filter first and then executes the prompt for eligible records. This approach reduces unnecessary executions and helps optimize Copilot credit consumption.

claims.claim: Input tokens contribute to prompt-run cost.
claims.quote: The combination of input tokens, output tokens, and the model version allows you to compute the cost of your prompt run.

claims.claim: Output tokens contribute to prompt-run cost, so longer output can increase consumption.
claims.quote: Output tokens refer to the tokens generated by the model in its response. This includes tokens from both the reasoning process and the final result produced by the prompt.

claims.claim: The model version contributes to prompt-run cost.
claims.quote: The combination of input tokens, output tokens, and the model version allows you to compute the cost of your prompt run.

claims.claim: The cost rating is variable because prompt execution is credit-metered.
claims.quote: Prompt columns consume credits every time a prompt is executed. Copilot Credits are a common currency for eligible Microsoft services with usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Prompt-column prerequisites require the environment's Copilot feature to be on.
claims.quote: Copilot and AI Prompts features turned On in the Features area for the environment settings.

claims.claim: Prompt-column prerequisites require the environment's AI Prompts feature to be on.
claims.quote: Copilot and AI Prompts features turned On in the Features area for the environment settings.

claims.claim: A table can have up to five prompt columns.
claims.quote: You can create up to five prompt columns per table.

claims.claim: Block unmanaged customizations must be disabled to create or edit prompt columns.
claims.quote: To create or edit Prompt Columns, the‘Block unmanaged customizations’ environment setting must be disabled.

claims.claim: The general AI prompts feature is enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, the AI prompts feature is enabled for makers to create and experiment with various AI-generated content.

claims.claim: Changing environment feature settings requires the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions.
claims.quote: Ensure you have the System Administrator security role or equivalent permissions to update the settings.

claims.claim: The AI prompts setting is reached through Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > AI Builder > AI prompts.
claims.quote:
select Environments > [select an environment] > Settings > Product > Features.
On the Features settings page under AI Builder, enable or disable the AI prompts toggle.

claims.claim: PATCH /api/data/v9.2/organizations(<organizationid>) updates the organization record containing the AI prompts control.
claims.quote:
Entity set path:
[organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/organizations
Primary key:
organizationid
Operations supported:
GETPATCH

claims.claim: The request body sets the Boolean aipromptsenabled property to enable or disable AI prompts.
claims.quote: aipromptsenabled | Edm.Boolean | Indicates whether AI Prompts feature is enabled. Display name: Enable AI Prompts.

claims.claim: An AI prompts environment group rule governs AI prompts availability for the group.
claims.quote: If your environment is part of an environment group, you can also govern AI prompts feature availability through the AI prompts environment group rule.

claims.claim: Publishing the AI prompts group rule locks the environment-level setting, which must then be changed through the group rule.
claims.quote: If an environment group rule governing AI prompts is published, it locks the AI prompts setting at the environment-level, preventing any system administrator of those individual environments from editing the setting.

claims.claim: The per-column execution control is at Power Apps > Tables > table > Columns > column > Edit column > Allow prompt column execution.
claims.quote:
Open the table, select Columns, and then open the column that is of data type Prompt where you want to disable AI generation.
On the Edit column pane, clear the Allow prompt column execution checkbox

claims.claim: Allow prompt column execution is enabled by default.
claims.quote: By default, the Allow prompt column execution setting is enabled.

claims.where: controls[1].governs; controls[1].note; Governance guidance: At rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Clearing Allow prompt column execution disables AI analysis for that individual column.
claims.quote: When disabled, AI analysis isn't performed for the prompt column.

claims.claim: An API or command for Allow prompt column execution is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow prompt column execution" API property Dataverse; "prompt column" "Allow prompt column execution" PowerShell REST metadata. Opened Prompt columns, Specialized columns using code and AI Configuration reference; no setting operation found.

claims.claim: Insufficient permission on an input column is a documented cause of prompt-column generation failure.
claims.quote: The user doesn't have sufficient permissions on one or more input columns referenced in the prompt column definition.

claims.claim: Learn states that on-demand prompt-column execution is not currently supported.
claims.quote: Prompt columns are triggered automatically on record updates; however, on‑demand execution is not currently supported.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises human review of generated content before using it to inform a business decision.
claims.quote: A human should review the content before you post it online, send it to a customer, or use it to inform a business decision.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Prompt columns are not audited.
claims.quote:
Are prompt columns audited?
Prompt columns aren't audited.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: Creating a prompt column automatically adds corresponding Status and Details columns.
claims.quote: When a prompt column is created, the table automatically includes two corresponding columns, Status and Details, for that prompt column.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The supporting columns record prompt execution status.
claims.quote: When prompt execution starts, these columns are populated to record the execution status and any failure details.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Details column records prompt execution failure details.
claims.quote: The prompt AI generation failed. Detail column shows error details in the last execution.

claims.claim: Learn states that both tenant-level and column-level settings must be enabled for prompts to execute.
claims.quote: For prompts to be executed, both tenant level and column level settings need to be enabled.

claims.claim: The AI prompts and column execution controls govern prompt columns generally.
claims.quote:
Common scenarios where the prompt doesn't execute, no error is surfaced, and execution is skipped:
AI Prompt feature is disabled.
Prompt column execution is disabled.

claims.claim: Learn does not specifically tie the two general prompt-column controls to multi-line output.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" licensing default switch; "prompt columns" "multi-line" admin existing licensing rollout. Read Prompt columns and Administer AI Builder; neither describes a multi-line-specific applicability statement.

claims.claim: The roadmap description mentions no new connector, identity or permission.
claims.quote: Prompt columns can now store multilple lines of text as prompt output, enabling longer and detailed AI-generated insights to be stored in your tables.

claims.claim: Prompt execution consumes the environment's AI credit capacity.
claims.quote: Once an environment has Copilot Credits available, it can run the AI Builder features in all contexts. If an environment only has AI Builder credits available, it can only run AI Builder features in Power Apps and Power Automate.

claims.claim: The prompt designer has a Test option for testing against real table data before saving.
claims.quote:
When you create a prompt column, you can test the prompt against real data in your table before you save it.
Run the default test. In the prompt designer, select Test.

claims.claim: Makers can test a prompt on different table records.
claims.quote: Test a different record. Open the text input variable (PromptColumnRecordId by default) and enter the record ID of the record you want to test as the sample value.

claims.claim: The supporting Status and Details columns can be displayed with table records for monitoring.
claims.quote:
Search and select the columns named:
(columnName) _PromptColumnStatus
(columnName)_PromptColumnDetails
Select Save.
Select Edit to the right of the list to open the columns list with records in a separate view.

claims.claim: No licensing information specific to the multi-line output enhancement is published.
claims.quote: Searched: "prompt columns" "multiple lines" licensing default switch; "prompt columns" "multi-line" admin existing licensing rollout. Opened Prompt columns, Overview of prompts, Overview of licensing and Prompt tokens; only general prompt licensing was found.
